title: Act on the Honorable Treatment of Former Presidents
full_text:
ACT ON THE HONORABLE TREATMENT OF FORMER PRESIDENTS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to prescribe matters concerning the honorable treatment of former Presidents.

Article 2 (Definition)
The term "former President" in this Act means a person who was elected President in accordance with the Constitution and served as President.

Article 3 (Scope of Application)
This Act shall apply to former Presidents and their surviving family members.

Article 3-2
Deleted on December 29, 1995.

Article 4 (Pensions)
(1) A pension shall be paid to a former President.
(2) The amount of the pension under paragraph (1) shall be an amount equivalent to 95/100 of the annual remuneration of the incumbent President at the time of payment.

Article 5 (Survivors' Pensions)
(1) A survivors' pension shall be paid to the spouse of a former President among the former President's surviving family members, in an amount equivalent to 70/100 of the annual remuneration of the incumbent President at the time of payment.
(2) Where a former President has no surviving spouse, or the spouse receiving a survivors' pension under paragraph (1) dies, that pension shall be paid to surviving children of the former President who are under 30 years of age and to surviving children aged 30 or older who are incapable of earning a livelihood. Where two or more persons are eligible, the pension shall be divided equally among them.

Article 5-2 (Support for Commemorative Projects)
Where private organizations, etc., undertake commemorative projects for a former President, necessary support may be provided as prescribed by the relevant statutes and regulations.

Article 5-3 (Support for Grave Management)
Where a former President has died and has not been buried in a national cemetery, personnel and expenses necessary for managing the grave may be provided as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 6 (Other Forms of Honorable Treatment)
(1) A former President may have three secretaries and one driver. Where a former President has died, his or her spouse may have one secretary and one driver.
(2) Secretaries and drivers whom a former President may have under paragraph (1) shall be appointed from among persons recommended by the former President. The secretaries shall be public officials in special service belonging to the Senior Executive Service, and the driver shall be a public official in special service.
(3) Secretaries and drivers whom the spouse of a deceased former President may have under paragraph (1) shall be appointed from among persons recommended by that spouse, and their status shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(4) The following forms of honorable treatment may be provided to a former President or the former President's surviving family members as prescribed by the relevant statutes and regulations:
1. Personal protection and security for a necessary period;
2. Support, including transportation, communications and provision of office space;
3. Medical treatment for the former President or surviving family member and his or her family;
4. Other forms of honorable treatment necessary for a former President.

Article 7 (Suspension and Exclusion of Rights, etc.)
(1) Where a person eligible for the application of this Act assumes public office, payment of the pension under Articles 4 and 5 shall be suspended during the period in which that person holds public office.
(2) Where a former President falls under any of the following, no honorable treatment as a former President under this Act shall be provided, except for the treatment prescribed in Article 6 (4) 1:
1. Where the former President left office following an impeachment decision during his or her term;
2. Where a sentence of imprisonment without labor or a heavier punishment has become final and conclusive;
3. Where the former President requested refuge or protection from a foreign government for the purpose of evading criminal proceedings;
4. Where the former President has lost nationality of the Republic of Korea.

Article 8 (Prohibition of Duplicate Pension Payments)
No pension under any other Act shall be paid to a person receiving a pension under this Act.

Article 9 (Methods and Procedures for Payment of Pensions)
Methods and procedures for paying pensions under this Act and other matters necessary for the enforcement of this Act shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

ADDENDUM <Act No. 2086, January 22, 1969>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation and shall apply to former Presidents and their surviving family members since the establishment of the Government of the Republic of Korea.

ADDENDUM <Act No. 3378, March 2, 1981>

(1) (Enforcement Date) This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

(2) (Transitional Measures) For three months after this Act enters into force, remuneration for the former secretaries of former Presidents employed pursuant to former Article 5 as at the time this Act enters into force shall continue to be borne by the National Treasury under the former provisions: Provided, That, if a secretary is appointed under this Act before the expiration of that period, the National Treasury shall cease to bear the remuneration of a former secretary corresponding to the rank of the newly appointed secretary.

ADDENDUM <Act No. 4001, February 24, 1988>

This Act shall enter into force on February 25, 1988.

ADDENDUM <Act No. 5118, December 29, 1995>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDUM (State Public Officials Act) <Act No. 7796, December 29, 2005>

Article 1 (Enforcement Date)
This Act shall enter into force on July 1, 2006.

Articles 2 through 5
Omitted.

Article 6 (Amendments to Other Acts)
(1) through (52) Omitted.

(53) The Honorable Treatment of Ex-Presidents Act shall be partially amended as follows:

In Article 6 (2), "one shall be a public official in special service of the State equivalent to Grade I and two shall be public officials in special service of the State equivalent to Grade II" shall be replaced with "public officials in special service belonging to the Senior Executive Service".

(54) through (68) Omitted.

ADDENDUM <Act No. 10011, February 4, 2010>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDUM <Act No. 10742, May 30, 2011>

This Act shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation.

ADDENDUM <Act No. 14618, March 21, 2017>

This Act shall enter into force on the date six months after its promulgation.

metadata.completion_statement: Complete English text of every provision of Articles 1 through 9, including Articles 3-2, 5-2 and 5-3, plus all eight Addenda. The existing twenty applicable English reference units were reused and joined in their original section order. Deleted and omitted provisions and all enforcement notes are preserved. Annexes and forms are excluded.
